intake: believer - practicing Roman Catholic, weekly Mass and confession, reads Aquinas; hold that God is ipsum esse subsistens and also personal (intellect and will), with faith that has been through a PhD's worth of doubt and come out the other side.

walk.note: This is how I came to faith too, as an inherited story that explained things; the story later had to earn its keep, but the move is honest about where everyone starts.
I hold classical theism alongside religion rather than instead of it, and 'written by man' is no scandal to a Catholic (inspired human authors), but the move does land me where I already stand.

Classical theism does not deny a personal God; Aquinas derives intellect, will and free action from the first cause (ST I qq.14, 19), so 'a first cause is not a God who acts' and 'the personal God that classical theism denies' misdescribe the position being left.

Granting agnosticism, the premise that a God who acts must show up as a statistical correlation in a prayer study treats petition as a mechanism, which is not what any serious theology of prayer claims; and the hiddenness horn reuses move 3's mistake.
Granting atheism, I agree the mind does not seem to reduce to matter; I would land in hylomorphism rather than Descartes, but the position is defined broadly enough to hold me.

I grant that mind depends on the brain and changes with it, and Elisabeth's objection bites a Cartesian ghost; but dependence is not identity, and the move itself later concedes at move 8 that physics gives structure, not what has it.
Granting materialism, this is a fair widening of the term.

I accept that physics describes only structure, but that gets you to 'something has the structure,' not to 'reality is at bottom experience'; Russellian monism, neutral monism, or classical theism are all open from the same premise.
Granting Dream, a dream wants a dreamer and the cogito gets you a subject; though the brushing-off of a cosmic dreamer leans on moves 3 and 4, which I refused.
Strawson's point is sound, and other persons are not in doubt for me.

I would ground it in the dignity of persons rather than a bare choice, and for me treating others well is owed, which her definition excludes from mercy; but she allows that a system crossing through duty has still crossed, so I cross.
Augustine and Cusa are home ground; the entropy aside is odd but does not break the step.
Second naivete is where I actually live; I get here with far less machinery than the replaceability apparatus, but the author says plainly that hope is a choice, and I make it.
Aquinas does hold God knows in a single act and forgets nothing; I take it while noting that 'resolved' is doing work the move itself half-retracts in its last sentence.
'More of a bargain than an argument' tells me nothing about what was bargained or why; there is no content here to take.

'To think is to ignore' is true of finite attention and is simply asserted of every possible mind; the move itself concedes Aquinas's non-discursive knowing has not been shown incoherent, which is the whole question.
Granting no maker, goods really are in beings (goodness is convertible with being), so the good does not vanish; the critics' grounding question is the one I would press, but the step itself is fair.

Granting the previous position, continuity has to be carried some way, and the move is honest that the need is a motive for the question rather than evidence; since the position is openly a question, arriving at the question is arriving there.
The text does not take this move and says there is no data; I would not wait on data about a system that does not exist to settle what I already hold about persistence, so I do not take it either.

first_exit.why: The move leaves classical theism on a description Aquinas would not recognize: he derives intellect, will and personal action from the first cause, and classical theism denies that God is a being among beings, not that God is personal. The dilemma about hiddenness therefore has no bite on the position it claims to refute.

comment: Your two exits from theism, moves 3 and 16, both rest on a description of classical theism that Aquinas would not sign: he derives a God who knows, wills and acts from the first cause, and your own text concedes at move 16 that his non-discursive knowing has not been shown incoherent. Repair those two and the route either stays in theism or has to find a different door out. The second turn, especially moves 11 through 13, is a stretch I would gladly walk with you, and I think you have more company there than you expect.
